pr_title: fix: fix sourcemap when using object as `define` value
pr_body:
### Description

- Closes https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/15771

I wrote my findings in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/15771#issuecomment-1926021038. The issue seems to be esbuild including multiple `sources` in source map when it cannot replace "define" value with primitive ([esbuild example](https://esbuild.github.io/try/#dAAwLjIwLjAAewogIHNvdXJjZW1hcDogdHJ1ZSwKICBkZWZpbmU6IHsKICAgICJpbXBvcnQubWV0YS5lbnYiOiAieyBcIlNTUlwiOiBmYWxzZSB9IiwKICAgICJpbXBvcnQubWV0YS5lbnYuU1NSIjogImZhbHNlIgogIH0sCn0AZnVuY3Rpb24gbWFpbigpIHsKICBjb25zb2xlLmxvZygnaGVsbG8nLCBpbXBvcnQubWV0YS5lbnYuVklURV9OT1RfRVhJU1QpOwp9CgptYWluKCk)) while later pipeline for source map collapsing/remapping doesn't expect such extra `sources` entries.

Since it doesn't look possible to control how esbuild output source entries, I think one way to "fix" this issue is to simply remove all extra source map entries which doesn't correspond to the original source. In this PR, I attempted this approach by using utilities from `@jridgewell/trace-mapping` (which is mostly re-exports of `@jridgewell/sourcemap-codec`).

issue_context.title: sourcemap is invalid when environment variables do not exist
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

In the vitejs 5.0.12 documentation it was mentioned that environment variables would be replaced with undefined if they didn't exist, what I didn't expect was that this made sourcemap invalid. Maybe this is a feature rather than a bug. If that's the case, then I think it should be mentioned in the documentation, this saves developers time in locating problems.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-om3cbj?file=README.md&terminal=dev

### Steps to reproduce

1. open the project using vscode
2. `npm run build:env-sourcemap`
3. add a breakpoint in the ./src/env-not-exist.ts file
4. open vscode javascript debugging terminal
5. `node ./dist/env-not-exist.cjs`
6. breakpoint not in effect
7. repeat the above steps in ./dist/ env-existence.cjs and./src/env-exist.ts, no problem

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: macOS 13.0
    CPU: (8) arm64 Apple M1
    Memory: 63.05 MB / 8.00 GB
    Shell: 5.8.1 - /bin/zsh
  Binaries:
    Node: 16.18.0 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v16.18.0/bin/node
    Yarn: 1.22.10 - /usr/local/bin/yarn
    npm: 8.19.4 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v16.18.0/bin/npm
    pnpm: 8.10.2 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v16.18.0/bin/pnpm
  Browsers:

  npmPackages:
    @vitejs/plugin-vue: ^4.5.2 => 4.6.2
```


### Used Package Manager

comments: _Start a new pull request in [StackBlitz Codeflow](https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/15771?repros=vitejs-vite-om3cbj)._ - [**vitejs-vite-om3cbj** (Open reproduction)](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-om3cbj?issueRepo=vitejs/vite&issueNumber=15771) Thanks for the reproduction. Indeed, source map seems broken when referencing non-existing `import.meta.env` keys in the code. I don't think this behavior is particularly intended (though it might be a technical limitation), so let me treat it as a bug. (I also made a reproduction for non-lib build https://github.com/hi-ogawa/repro-vite-sourcemap-bad-meta-env and SSR dev https://github.com/hi-ogawa/repro-vite-ssr-error-stack/pull/1) From my investigation so far, I'm suspecting that this is caused by esbuild's source map including `` as an extra entry in `sources` (and main source being end up in 2nd entry): - [esbuild example 1](https://esbuild.github.io/try/#dAAwLjIwLjAAewogIHNvdXJjZW1hcDogdHJ1ZSwKICBkZWZpbmU6IHsKICAgICJpbXBvcnQubWV0YS5lbnYiOiAieyBcIlNTUlwiOiBmYWxzZSB9IiwKICAgICJpbXBvcnQubWV0YS5lbnYuU1NSIjogImZhbHNlIgogIH0sCn0AZnVuY3Rpb24gbWFpbigpIHsKICBjb25zb2xlLmxvZygnaGVsbG8nLCBpbXBvcnQubWV0YS5lbnYuVklURV9OT1RfRVhJU1QpOwp9CgptYWluKCk) ```json { "version": 3, "sources": ["", ""], "sourcesContent": ["", "function main() {\n console.log('hello', import.meta.env.VITE_NOT_EXIST);\n}\n\nmain()"], "mappings": "AAAA,uCAAE,KAAO,MAAM;ACAf,SAAS,OAAO;AACd,UAAQ,IAAI,SAAS,+BAAgB,cAAc;AACrD;AAEA,KAAK;", "names": [] } ``` This doesn't seem to happen when `import.meta.env.XXX` keys are properly replaced as a primitive, for example: - [esbuild example 2](https://esbuild.github.io/try/#dAAwLjIwLjAAewogIHNvdXJjZW1hcDogdHJ1ZSwKICBkZWZpbmU6IHsKICAgICJpbXBvcnQubWV0YS5lbnYiOiAieyBcIlNTUlwiOiBmYWxzZSB9IiwKICAgICJpbXBvcnQubWV0YS5lbnYuU1NSIjogImZhbHNlIgogIH0sCn0AZnVuY3Rpb24gbWFpbigpIHsKICBjb25zb2xlLmxvZygnaGVsbG8nLCBpbXBvcnQubWV0YS5lbnYuU1NSKTsKfQoKbWFpbigp) I'm not familiar with how rollup combines multiple source maps from transform pipeline, but I think they don't expect there'll be multiple sources referenced from a single transform (as their doc mentions they only use `mappings` property https://rollupjs.org/plugin-development/#source-code-transformations). To fix this, (assuming esbuild doesn't support controlling `sources` output) I think it's technically possible to manipulate esbuild's source map output and filter out all `` related mapping segments and that'll probably save main source's mapping to be usable. > Thanks for the reproduction.
